Title: Expense on P-1040 billed at thirteen times its cost
Repro Steps:
1. Open project P-1040, which has a 12% expense markup.
2. Create a proposal for October with the approved hotel expense of 250.00 EUR.
3. Look at the expense line.
Expected: 280.00
Actual: 3,250.00
Resolution: The markup was stored as a fraction (0.12) in 4.0 and the migration converted it to a percentage (12). ExpenseWithMarkup still multiplied by the value directly. It now divides by 100.

Title: No VAT on invoices to Finnish customers
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for any Finnish business customer with a VAT number (for example Halden, P-1001).
2. Look at the tax column.
Expected: S 24%
Actual: RC with 0.00 tax and the reverse charge note
Resolution: IsReverseCharge treated every EU business customer with a VAT number as reverse charged, including customers in Finland. It now also checks that the customer's country differs from the company's.

Title: Due date one day earlier than the payment terms
Repro Steps:
1. Finalise an invoice dated 31 Oct for a customer with 30 day terms.
Expected: due 30 Nov
Actual: due 29 Nov
Resolution: DueDate subtracted a day from the terms (carried over from the 4.0 report logic, which counted the invoice date as day one).

Title: Amounts shown without thousand separators
Repro Steps:
1. Open any invoice over 1,000 EUR.
Expected: 2,447.25 EUR
Actual: 2447.25 EUR
Resolution: FormatMoney and FormatAmount now use the #,##0.00 pattern.

Title: Non-billable internal time appears on customer invoices
Repro Steps:
1. On P-1001, record 2 h of internal time with Billable unticked and approve it.
2. Create a proposal for the period.
Expected: the internal time is not on the proposal
Actual: it is billed at the consultant's rate
Resolution: The time entry query in CreateProposal did not filter on Billable. Added the condition.

Title: Credit note numbers not padded like invoice numbers
Repro Steps:
1. Issue a credit note.
Expected: CN-000004
Actual: CN-4
Resolution: The credit note branch in NumberingService did not format the number. Both sequences now use six digits.

Title: Error when crediting an invoice migrated from 4.0
Repro Steps:
1. Open invoice INV-000112 (migrated from TFS, EUR, no exchange rate stored).
2. Create credit note, enter 100.00 on line 1, give a reason and issue.
Expected: credit note issued
Actual: error page (Nullable object must have a value)
Resolution: Invoices migrated from 4.0 have no exchange rate. The credit line now keeps the amount as the company-currency value when the rate is missing or zero.

Title: Final invoice can be deleted
Repro Steps:
1. Finalise a proposal.
2. Open /Proposals/Edit/<id> for the invoice from the browser history and press Delete proposal.
Expected: refused
Actual: the invoice is deleted and its time goes back to unbilled
Resolution: ProposalService.Delete did not check the status. A final invoice is now refused with a pointer to credit notes.

Title: UK customers reverse charged after Brexit
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Brightline Ltd (GB, VAT number GB...).
Expected: no reverse charge note, export treatment as configured
Actual: RC and the EU reverse charge wording
Resolution: The country list came from 4.0 and still had GB. Removed.

Title: Empty brackets after time line descriptions
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal where a time entry has no comment.
Expected: 2023-11-02 Pekka Salo - CONS
Actual: 2023-11-02 Pekka Salo - CONS ()
Resolution: The comment is only added when there is one.

Title: VAT not updated after a write-up
Repro Steps:
1. On a proposal, write line 1 up by 100.00 with a reason.
Expected: tax on line 1 rises by 24.00
Actual: amount changes, tax stays the same
Resolution: Recalculate passed the unadjusted source amount to the tax calculation. Amount and tax now use the same adjusted value.

Title: Halden billed at rate card instead of agreed rate
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for P-1003 (Halden support retainer).
2. Look at senior consultant time.
Expected: 140.00 (Halden agreement)
Actual: 155.00 (project rate card)
Resolution: ResolveRate looked at the project rate card first. The customer agreement is now checked first, as in the contract terms.

Title: Private customer invoiced without VAT
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for a private customer in Sweden that has a personal tax number entered in the VAT field.
Expected: Finnish VAT
Actual: reverse charge
Resolution: Reverse charge applies to business customers only. IsReverseCharge now checks IsBusiness first.

Title: Submitted time billed before the project manager approved it
Repro Steps:
1. On P-1001, submit 4 h for the period but do not approve it.
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: the submitted entry is not billed
Actual: it is on the proposal
Resolution: The query excluded rejected entries only, so draft and submitted entries were billed. It now takes approved entries only.

Title: Billing hold message does not say which customer
Repro Steps:
1. Put Ostra Logistics on hold with a reason.
2. Create a proposal for P-1120.
Expected: Billing hold: customer Ostra Logistics Oy is on hold. <reason>
Actual: Customer C140 is on billing hold.
Resolution: The message now gives the customer name and the hold reason.

Title: Ledger rejects invoices with long PO numbers
Repro Steps:
1. Enter a 40 character purchase order number on a proposal and finalise.
Expected: validation message
Actual: invoice finalised, ledger posting fails overnight
Resolution: The ledger PO field is 30 characters. IsValidPoNumber now rejects longer values.

Title: Fixed-price milestone billed again the next month
Repro Steps:
1. P-1080: bill the completed milestone Solution design in January and finalise.
2. Create the February proposal.
Expected: no milestone line
Actual: Solution design billed again
Resolution: Finalise now records the invoice on each milestone it bills, and proposals skip milestones that already have an invoice.

Title: Header shows the calendar date instead of the business date
Repro Steps:
1. Set Billing:BusinessDate to 2024-01-31 during the January run.
2. Look at the header on 1 Feb.
Expected: Business date 31 Jan 2024
Actual: 1 Feb 2024
Resolution: The layout used DateTime.Today. It now reads the SystemClock like the rest of the application.

Title: Two invoices got the same number
Repro Steps:
1. Two billing clerks finalise proposals at the same moment (seen in the January run: INV-000041 twice).
Expected: consecutive numbers
Actual: duplicate number
Resolution: NumberingService read and incremented the counter without a lock. Allocation is now serialised and the company row is reloaded before use.

Title: Due date counted from the day of finalising
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal with invoice date 31 Jan, finalise it on 2 Feb.
Expected: due 1 Mar (31 Jan + 30)
Actual: due 3 Mar
Resolution: Finalise passed the business date to DueDate. It now passes the invoice date.

Title: Credit note can be issued without a reason
Repro Steps:
1. Open a final invoice, Create credit note.
2. Enter 50.00 on line 1, leave Reason empty, issue.
Expected: Enter a reason for the credit note.
Actual: credit note issued with the note 'Credit for invoice INV-000057. '
Resolution: A reason is now required, and it is trimmed before it goes on the credit note.

Title: Period end shown as 28 February in a leap year
Repro Steps:
1. Open New proposal on 29 Feb 2024.
Expected: period end 2024-02-29
Actual: 2024-02-28, and time entered on the 29th is left out
Resolution: EndOfMonth had a fixed table of month lengths. It now uses DateTime.DaysInMonth.

Title: Invoice date defaults to the business date, not the period end
Repro Steps:
1. On 4 March, open New proposal.
Expected: period end 2024-03-31, invoice date 2024-03-31
Actual: invoice date 2024-03-04, which then fails 'The invoice date cannot be before the period end'
Resolution: The page defaults the invoice date to the period end.

Title: Missing exchange rate silently treated as 1.0
Repro Steps:
1. Delete the SEK rate for March (or create a proposal before it is entered).
2. Create a proposal for a SEK customer.
Expected: a clear warning that the rate is missing
Actual: SEK amounts equal to the EUR amounts, no warning
Resolution: The proposal keeps an empty rate instead of 1.0, the page shows a warning banner and 'Missing' in the rate field.

Title: Invoice export fails when credit notes are in the list
Repro Steps:
1. Invoices, search for Lumo, press Export.
Expected: CSV file
Actual: error page
Resolution: Credit notes have no due date. The export now leaves the field empty.

Title: Amounts with a thousand separator are rejected
Repro Steps:
1. On a credit note, enter 1,480.00 for line 1.
Expected: accepted
Actual: '1,480.00' is not a valid amount.
Resolution: ParseMoney removes spaces and commas before parsing.

Title: Invoice line 0.5 cent amounts round down to even
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for a SEK customer where a line converts to 1,234.565 SEK.
Expected: 1,234.57
Actual: 1,234.56 (and 1,234.575 gives 1,234.58)
Resolution: Math.Round defaults to banker's rounding. RoundMoney now rounds half away from zero, as finance and the customer's AP systems expect.

Title: Reverse charge note lacks the legal reference
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Atlas (DE, VAT number).
Expected: wording with the directive article, as required by the German customer's AP
Actual: 'Reverse charge.'
Resolution: The note now carries the full wording.

Title: April exchange rate used on March invoices
Repro Steps:
1. Enter the GBP rate effective 1 April on 26 March.
2. Create a March proposal for a GBP customer.
Expected: the March rate
Actual: the April rate
Resolution: GetRate took the newest rate regardless of its effective date. It now takes the latest rate on or before the date.

Title: Invoice quantity shows recorded hours but bills quarter hours
Repro Steps:
1. Record 1.10 h on P-1001 and create a proposal.
Expected: quantity 1.25, amount 1.25 x rate
Actual: quantity 1.10, amount 1.25 x rate, so the line does not add up
Resolution: The line quantity is now the rounded hours that are billed.

Title: Credit note dated in the original invoice's period
Repro Steps:
1. Credit a January invoice in April.
Expected: credit note dated in April
Actual: dated in January, a closed ledger period, posting fails
Resolution: Credit notes take the business date as their invoice date.

Title: User switch redirects to any address in returnUrl
Repro Steps:
1. POST /User/Switch with returnUrl=https://example.org.
Expected: back to the home page
Actual: redirected to the external site
Resolution: The switch uses LocalRedirect and falls back to the home page for anything not local.

Title: Expenses stay reserved after a proposal is deleted
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for P-1040 with an expense line, delete the proposal.
2. Create the proposal again.
Expected: the expense is on it
Actual: time is back, the expense is missing
Resolution: Delete released time entries only. It now releases expenses too.

Title: Agreement discount of 150% accepted
Repro Steps:
1. Customers, open C100, enter 150 as discount and save.
Expected: rejected
Actual: saved, next proposal has negative time lines
Resolution: The discount must be between 0 and 50%, the maximum in the price policy.

Title: PO of a single space accepted for PO customers
Repro Steps:
1. Meridian requires a PO. Enter a space as PO number and finalise.
Expected: A purchase order number is required
Actual: finalised, customer rejects the invoice
Resolution: Finalise now uses IsValidPoNumber instead of an empty check.

Title: Correcting a rate adds a second rate for the same day
Repro Steps:
1. Exchange rates, save SEK 11.40 effective 2024-04-01, then save 11.45 for the same date.
Expected: one rate, 11.45
Actual: two rates, invoices pick either
Resolution: Saving a rate for a date that already has one now updates it.

Title: Final invoice of a closing project deferred as too small
Repro Steps:
1. Set P-1090 to Closing with 30.00 EUR of unbilled time.
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: proposal for 30.00
Actual: deferred, and the project cannot be closed
Resolution: A closing project gets its last invoice regardless of the minimum.

Title: Amounts wrap onto two lines in narrow columns
Repro Steps:
1. Open a proposal on a laptop screen.
Expected: 1,234.50 EUR on one line
Actual: currency code wraps under the amount
Resolution: Number cells no longer wrap.

Title: Converted amounts off by a cent on large SEK invoices
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Nordvik (SEK) with a line of 12,345.67 EUR at rate 11.4523.
Expected: 141,385.32 SEK
Actual: 141,385.31 SEK
Resolution: Convert went through double, which loses precision. It now multiplies in decimal.

Title: June expenses billed on the May invoice
Repro Steps:
1. Approve an expense dated 3 June on P-1040.
2. Create a proposal with period end 31 May.
Expected: not included
Actual: included
Resolution: The expense query had no period end condition. Added.

Title: Due date equals invoice date for customers without terms
Repro Steps:
1. Customer C170 has payment terms 0 (not set in the migration).
2. Finalise an invoice.
Expected: due 30 days after the invoice date
Actual: due on the invoice date
Resolution: Customers without payment terms get the 30 day default.

Title: Deferred proposal can be finalised
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal under 50 EUR (deferred).
2. Post to the Finalise handler of that proposal.
Expected: refused
Actual: invoice for 12.00 EUR finalised
Resolution: Finalise refuses deferred proposals.

Title: Milestone completed on the last day not billed
Repro Steps:
1. During the May run (business date 31 May), on 3 June mark a P-1080 milestone complete.
2. Create the May proposal.
Expected: the milestone is billed
Actual: it is completed on 3 June, after the period end, and left out
Resolution: Mark complete now uses the business date.

Title: Negative credit amount increases what the customer owes
Repro Steps:
1. Create a credit note and enter -100 on line 1.
Expected: rejected
Actual: a credit note with a positive amount is issued
Resolution: Credit amounts must be positive.

Title: Still open to credit shows more than the invoice total
Repro Steps:
1. Open INV-000291 (already credited by CN-000013) and press Create credit note.
Expected: Still open to credit 1,857.40 EUR
Actual: 4,116.40 EUR
Resolution: Credit note totals are negative, so subtracting them added to the open amount. CreditedSoFar now sums absolute values.

Title: Milestone billed before it was complete
Repro Steps:
1. P-1080: a milestone planned for 15 June is not complete yet.
2. Create the June proposal.
Expected: not billed
Actual: billed because its planned date has passed
Resolution: 4.0 billed milestones on their planned date. Only completed milestones are billed now.

Title: Finalise button shown on a final invoice
Repro Steps:
1. Open /Proposals/Edit/<id> for a final invoice.
Expected: locked banner, no Finalise or Delete buttons
Actual: both buttons shown (they fail with an error)
Resolution: The action buttons are only rendered for open proposals.

Title: Agreement discount taken off expenses
Repro Steps:
1. Set a 10% discount on Halden (C100).
2. Create a proposal for P-1002.
Expected: time lines discounted, expense line 120.00
Actual: expense line 108.00
Resolution: ApplyDiscount ignored the line kind. It now discounts time lines only.

Title: Credit notes take numbers from the invoice sequence
Repro Steps:
1. Issue a credit note.
Expected: CN-000014
Actual: INV-000188, and the next invoice skips a number
Resolution: CreateAsync asked for an invoice number. It now uses the credit note sequence.

Title: Reverse charge applied to EU customer without a VAT number
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for P-1060 (Lumo, DE, no VAT number on file).
Expected: Finnish VAT
Actual: RC, no VAT
Resolution: Without a VAT number the customer cannot account for the VAT. IsReverseCharge now requires one.

Title: Proposal totals shown under the adjustment column
Repro Steps:
1. Open any proposal.
Expected: Subtotal, Tax and Total under Amount
Actual: one column to the left
Resolution: The footer colspan did not count the Adjustment column.

Title: Gaps in invoice numbers after deleting proposals
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal (number INV-000190 shown), delete it.
2. Create and finalise another.
Expected: INV-000190
Actual: INV-000191, the auditors flagged the gap
Resolution: Proposals took a number when they were created. The number is now given when the invoice is finalised, and the proposal shows 'Assigned when finalised'.

Title: Project on billing hold still invoiced
Repro Steps:
1. Put P-1011 on billing hold (disputed hours).
2. Create a proposal for it.
Expected: Billing hold: project P-1011 is on hold.
Actual: proposal created
Resolution: Only the customer hold was checked. The project hold is checked too.

Title: Write-down can take a line below zero
Repro Steps:
1. Write line 1 (500.00) down by 600.00 with a reason.
Expected: refused
Actual: line -100.00
Resolution: A write-down cannot be larger than the line.

Title: Credit note one cent short of the invoice line
Repro Steps:
1. Credit 99.995 GBP equivalent on a GBP invoice line (full credit of a converted line).
Expected: -100.00
Actual: -99.99, leaving 0.01 open on the invoice
Resolution: CreditAmount truncated to two decimals. It now uses the same rounding as invoice lines.

Title: Reverse charge note missing from the proposal
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Atlas (P-1050).
Expected: the reverse charge note under the header
Actual: no note; it only appears on the PDF
Resolution: The note from the tax result is now stored on the invoice when the proposal is created.

Title: Invoice credited twice over
Repro Steps:
1. INV-000291 has line 2 credited by CN-000013.
2. Create another credit note for both lines in full.
Expected: refused, only 1,857.40 EUR is still open
Actual: issued; the customer received 900.00 + tax twice
Resolution: The credit limit was the invoice total. It is now the total less what earlier credit notes have credited.

Title: Not-to-exceed limit reached too early
Repro Steps:
1. P-1030 has a not-to-exceed of 40,000 EUR, 32,000 invoiced and 4,000 credited.
2. Create a proposal with 6,000 EUR of time.
Expected: all time billed (28,000 + 6,000 is under the limit)
Actual: entries held back; open proposals and deferred proposals were also counted
Resolution: Billed to date now counts final invoices and subtracts final credit notes.

Title: Proposal does not say that entries were held back
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for a project close to its not-to-exceed limit.
Expected: a message that some entries were held back
Actual: entries silently missing
Resolution: The proposal stores how many entries were held back and the page shows the status reason as a banner.

Title: Cancelled invoice can be adjusted
Repro Steps:
1. Open a cancelled invoice from 4.0 in the proposal screen.
Expected: locked
Actual: lines can be adjusted
Resolution: IsLocked now covers cancelled invoices too.

Title: Time on the last day of the period left out
Repro Steps:
1. Record approved time on P-1001 on 31 August.
2. Create a proposal with period end 31 August.
Expected: included
Actual: left out, billed a month late
Resolution: The period end comparison was exclusive. It is now on or before.

Title: New 25.5% VAT rate shown as 26%
Repro Steps:
1. After the VAT change on 1 September, open a proposal or invoice.
Expected: S 25.5%
Actual: S 26% (amounts are right)
Resolution: Rates were formatted without decimals. Proposal, invoice and credit note pages now show up to two.

Title: Credit note for an August invoice charges 25.5% VAT
Repro Steps:
1. Credit an invoice from August 2024 (24% VAT).
Expected: credit note at 24%
Actual: 25.5%, today's rate for code S
Resolution: Credit lines took the current rate of the tax code. They now take the rate charged on the original line.

Title: Proposal fails for roles without a rate card entry
Repro Steps:
1. Add junior consultant time to P-1003 (no Halden or card rate for juniors).
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: billed at the standard junior rate 85.00
Actual: No rate found for role JUN on project P-1003.
Resolution: ResolveRate falls back to the role's standard rate.

Title: Credit note does not show which invoice it credits
Repro Steps:
1. Issue a credit note and open it.
Expected: 'Credits invoice INV-...' with a link
Actual: nothing
Resolution: The details page loads the original invoice and links to it.

Title: Invoice finalised in October uses October rate for a September invoice date
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal dated 30 Sep, finalise on 2 Oct after the October rate is entered.
Expected: September rate
Actual: October rate
Resolution: Finalise looked the rate up on the business date. It now uses the invoice date.

Title: Expenses billed over the not-to-exceed limit
Repro Steps:
1. P-1030 is 100 EUR under its limit; approve a 400 EUR expense.
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: the expense is held back
Actual: billed, limit exceeded
Resolution: The limit was only checked for time. Expenses are checked the same way.

Title: Proposal total shown without the currency
Repro Steps:
1. Open a proposal for a SEK customer.
Expected: Total 12,450.00 SEK
Actual: Total 12,450.00
Resolution: The total uses FormatMoney like the invoice page.

Title: SEK invoice finalised with EUR amounts
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for a SEK customer before the October rate is entered.
2. Finalise it.
Expected: refused until the rate is entered
Actual: finalised at 1.0, customer invoiced 1,500 SEK instead of 17,000 SEK
Resolution: Finalise stops with a message naming the currency and date when no rate is found.

Title: Adjust buttons shown on a final invoice
Repro Steps:
1. Open /Proposals/Edit/<id> for a final invoice.
Expected: no adjustment column
Actual: Adjust buttons on every line (they fail with an error)
Resolution: The adjustment column is only rendered for open proposals.

Title: One large entry stops all later time being billed
Repro Steps:
1. P-1030 has 900 EUR left under its limit. Time: 2 h, 8 h, 1 h.
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: the 8 h entry held back, the 1 h entry billed
Actual: both later entries held back
Resolution: The time loop stopped at the first entry over the limit. It now skips that entry and carries on.

Title: Credit line can exceed the invoice line
Repro Steps:
1. Credit 2,000.00 on a 1,480.00 line of an invoice that has other lines.
Expected: refused for the line
Actual: accepted as long as the invoice total is not exceeded
Resolution: Each line can be credited up to its own amount.

Title: Printed SEK lines do not add up to the invoice total
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Nordvik (SEK) with 14 time lines.
2. Add up the printed line amounts.
Expected: equal to the subtotal
Actual: 0.03 SEK different; the customer's AP rejected the invoice
Resolution: Lines were converted without rounding and only the total was rounded. Each line is now rounded in the invoice currency and the totals are the sum of the rounded lines.

Title: Short time entries rounded down to the quarter hour
Repro Steps:
1. Record 0.10 h (a six minute call) on P-1001.
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: 0.25 h billed
Actual: 0.00 h, line with zero amount
Resolution: Hours were rounded to the nearest quarter. They are rounded up, per the billing policy.

Title: Credit limit check ignores VAT
Repro Steps:
1. An invoice has 100.00 open including VAT.
2. Credit 90.00 before tax (112.95 with VAT).
Expected: refused
Actual: issued, invoice over-credited by 12.95
Resolution: The check compared the credit before tax with the open amount including tax. It now compares the credit total.

Title: Milestone billed on two proposals
Repro Steps:
1. Create a December proposal for P-1080 (completed milestone).
2. Create another one for the same project before finalising the first.
Expected: refused
Actual: second proposal with the same milestone; both were finalised
Resolution: A project can only have one open proposal.

Title: Saving an exchange rate without a date gives an error page
Repro Steps:
1. Exchange rates, enter a rate, leave the date empty, Save rate.
Expected: message asking for the date
Actual: error page
Resolution: The page checks the date before saving.

Title: Write-up saved without a reason
Repro Steps:
1. On a proposal, write line 1 up by 100 without a reason.
Expected: Enter a reason for the write-up.
Actual: saved; the customer queried the extra amount and nobody knew why
Resolution: Both write-ups and write-downs now need a reason.

Title: Interim billing above the contract value
Repro Steps:
1. On a pilot fixed-price project, cost to date exceeds the estimate.
2. Build the interim proposal.
Expected: billing stops at the contract value
Actual: 112% of the contract billed
Resolution: The completion percentage is capped at 100%.

Title: PO numbers in lower case rejected by the customer's AP
Repro Steps:
1. Enter po-4471 as purchase order on a Meridian proposal and finalise.
Expected: PO-4471 on the invoice
Actual: po-4471, rejected by Meridian's matching
Resolution: PO numbers are trimmed and upper-cased when saved, and an empty value no longer fails.

Title: Written-down proposal deferred as below minimum
Repro Steps:
1. Write a proposal up from 40 to 80 EUR.
Expected: proposal counted at 80 EUR
Actual: the subtotal used for the minimum and the not-to-exceed check stays at 40
Resolution: BaseSubtotal now includes write-ups and write-downs.

Title: Invoice amounts not updated to the final exchange rate
Repro Steps:
1. Create a GBP proposal before the month's rate is entered, enter the rate, finalise.
Expected: lines converted at the stored rate
Actual: rate on the invoice is new, amounts are still in EUR
Resolution: Finalise recalculates the lines after setting the rate.

Title: PO number can be changed on a final invoice
Repro Steps:
1. Post a PO change to a final invoice from an old browser tab.
Expected: refused
Actual: PO changed on the final invoice, different from the ledger
Resolution: SetPurchaseOrder refuses locked invoices.

Title: Empty credit note issued and numbered
Repro Steps:
1. Open Create credit note and press Issue without entering amounts.
Expected: Enter an amount to credit on at least one line.
Actual: CN-000031 issued for 0.00
Resolution: A credit note needs at least one line.

Title: Fixed-price projects listed with unbilled hours
Repro Steps:
1. Open Projects.
Expected: fixed-price projects show 0.00 unbilled hours
Actual: they show logged hours, which are never billed
Resolution: Fixed-price projects bill milestones, so the list shows 0.00 for them.

Title: Exempt invoices lack the exemption wording
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for the training project P-1095 (tax code E, exempt).
Expected: 0% and the exemption note
Actual: 0%, no note
Resolution: Exempt tax codes return a note with the code description.

Title: Write-down of 40% finalised without review
Repro Steps:
1. On a 12,000 EUR proposal for P-1001, write lines down by 4,800 EUR with a reason.
2. Finalise.
Expected: the proposal waits for a billing manager
Actual: finalised straight away; finance found it at month end
Resolution: Write-downs above 10% of the proposal now put it in Awaiting approval, and Finalise refuses it until a billing manager approves.

Title: Proposal stays awaiting approval after the write-down is removed
Repro Steps:
1. Write a proposal down by 20%, it goes to Awaiting approval.
2. Set the adjustment back to 0.
Expected: back to Proposal
Actual: still Awaiting approval
Resolution: When write-downs fall back under the limit the proposal returns to Proposal.

Title: Project manager can approve write-downs
Repro Steps:
1. Switch user to Sofia Berg (project manager).
2. Approvals, approve her own write-down.
Expected: refused
Actual: approved
Resolution: Approve and Reject check the billing manager role.

Title: Approvals list shows 0.00 written down
Repro Steps:
1. Open Approvals with one proposal waiting.
Expected: amounts before and written down
Actual: 0.00 and 0.00, no reasons
Resolution: The list query now loads the proposal lines.

Title: Status shown as PendingApproval
Repro Steps:
1. Open a proposal awaiting approval.
Expected: Status Awaiting approval
Actual: PendingApproval
Resolution: StatusLabel has a label for the new status.

Title: Second proposal created while the first awaits approval
Repro Steps:
1. P-1001 has a proposal awaiting approval.
2. Create another proposal for P-1001.
Expected: refused
Actual: created with the milestone and new time; both were finalised
Resolution: The open proposal check includes proposals awaiting approval.

Title: No message when a write-down sends the proposal for approval
Repro Steps:
1. Write a proposal down by 20%.
Expected: message that it now needs a billing manager's approval
Actual: 'Adjustment saved.'
Resolution: The message says when the proposal needs approval.

Title: Type filter on the invoice list shows everything
Repro Steps:
1. Invoices, choose Type: Credit notes, Search.
Expected: credit notes only
Actual: invoices and credit notes
Resolution: The list query ignored the type. It now filters on it when one is chosen.

Title: Customer with lower-case country code charged VAT
Repro Steps:
1. Customer C210 was imported with country 'de'.
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: reverse charge (German business with VAT number)
Actual: Finnish VAT
Resolution: IsEu upper-cases the country code before the lookup.

Title: Credit note lines in a different order from the invoice
Repro Steps:
1. Credit lines 1, 2 and 3 of a three-line invoice.
Expected: credit lines in the same order
Actual: sometimes 2, 1, 3
Resolution: The original invoice is loaded with its lines in sequence order.

Title: Totals unchanged after write-downs are rejected
Repro Steps:
1. Reject the write-downs on a proposal awaiting approval.
Expected: lines and totals back to the original amounts
Actual: lines show no adjustment but the total is still the written-down total
Resolution: Reject recalculates the proposal after clearing the write-downs.

Title: Yen invoices show decimals
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Kaito Systems (JPY).
Expected: amounts in whole yen
Actual: 152,340.47 JPY; the customer's bank rejected the payment reference
Resolution: MinorUnits returned 2 for every currency. JPY has none.

Title: Approval kept after a further write-down
Repro Steps:
1. A billing manager approves a 15% write-down.
2. The clerk writes another line down; total 30%.
Expected: Awaiting approval again
Actual: still approved, finalised at 30%
Resolution: Any write-down over the limit clears an earlier approval.

Title: Write-up reason not shown on the proposal
Repro Steps:
1. Write line 1 up with a reason.
Expected: reason shown under the line description
Actual: only visible in the audit log
Resolution: The proposal page shows the reason under the line.

Title: Interim billing counts open proposals as billed
Repro Steps:
1. Build an interim proposal, then build another before finalising the first.
Expected: second one bills the same amount
Actual: second one bills less, the open proposal counted as billed
Resolution: Billed to date counts final invoices only.

Title: Invoice list takes a minute to open
Repro Steps:
1. Open Invoices without a search.
Expected: list in a few seconds
Actual: about 60 s with 6,000 documents
Resolution: The page shows the latest 200 and says how many there are; search narrows the list.

Title: Exchange rate of zero accepted
Repro Steps:
1. Exchange rates, enter 0 for SEK and save.
Expected: refused
Actual: saved; proposals show 0.00 SEK
Resolution: The rate must be greater than zero.

Title: Credit amounts cleared after a validation error
Repro Steps:
1. Enter amounts on five lines, leave the reason empty, issue.
Expected: error, amounts still filled in
Actual: error, all fields empty
Resolution: The form shows the entered amounts and reason again.

Title: Purchase order form runs off the screen
Repro Steps:
1. Open a proposal on a 1366 px laptop.
Expected: PO form fits
Actual: Save PO button off screen
Resolution: Inline forms wrap.

Title: VAT on SEK invoices off by a few öre
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Nordvik (SEK) and check the VAT on each line.
Expected: VAT = rounded line amount x 25.5%, rounded
Actual: VAT worked out on the unrounded converted amount; 0.01 SEK out on some lines
Resolution: LineTax now converts and rounds the line first and works out the tax on that amount.

Title: Error page when a project has an unknown tax code
Repro Steps:
1. Project P-1097 has tax code S2 (removed).
2. Create a proposal.
Expected: message naming the tax code
Actual: error page
Resolution: TaxService reports the missing code.

Title: Error page when creating a proposal without a project
Repro Steps:
1. New proposal, leave Project empty, Create proposal.
Expected: Select a project.
Actual: error page
Resolution: The page asks for a project.

Title: Expense lines on the invoice have no date
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal with two hotel expenses.
Expected: each line starts with the expense date
Actual: only the description
Resolution: Expense lines start with the date, like time lines.

Title: Interim billing line shows 37.142857142857% complete
Repro Steps:
1. Build an interim proposal for a pilot project.
Expected: Progress billing 37.1% complete
Actual: 37.142857142857142857142857143%
Resolution: The percentage is rounded to one decimal in the description.

Title: Error page for a credit note link to a missing invoice
Repro Steps:
1. Open /CreditNotes/Create?invoiceId=999999.
Expected: Not found
Actual: error page
Resolution: The page returns Not found when the invoice does not exist.

Title: Home page counts projects with only non-billable time
Repro Steps:
1. Open the home page.
Expected: Projects with unbilled time counts billable time only
Actual: includes internal projects with non-billable time
Resolution: The tile counts billable time only.

Title: KRW and ISK invoices show decimals
Repro Steps:
1. Create a proposal for Hanseo Logistics (KRW) or Fjord Data ehf (ISK).
Expected: whole won / krónur
Actual: two decimals
Resolution: KRW and ISK have no minor units either. Added them next to JPY.

Title: Labels wrap in the proposal header
Repro Steps:
1. Open an approved proposal.
Expected: 'Write-downs approved by' on one line
Actual: wraps onto two lines
Resolution: The label column is wider.

Title: Interim billing fails with a division error
Repro Steps:
1. Build an interim proposal with an estimated cost of 0.
Expected: nothing to bill
Actual: error page (attempted to divide by zero)
Resolution: A zero or negative estimate gives nothing to bill.

Title: EUR offered on the exchange rate page
Repro Steps:
1. Open Exchange rates.
Expected: foreign currencies only
Actual: EUR is in the list and a EUR to EUR rate can be saved
Resolution: The company currency is left out of the list.

Title: Home page shows the business date as the period end
Repro Steps:
1. Open the home page on 9 June.
Expected: Billing period ending 30 June 2026
Actual: Billing period ending 9 June 2026
Resolution: The home page uses the end of the month.

Title: Audit log does not say whether a line was written up or down
Repro Steps:
1. Write a line down, open the audit log.
Expected: Write-down
Actual: Adjustment
Resolution: The audit action says Write-up or Write-down.

Title: Rate page jumps back to the first currency after saving
Repro Steps:
1. Exchange rates, choose SEK, save a rate.
Expected: SEK history shown
Actual: GBP history shown
Resolution: The redirect keeps the currency.

Title: Customer put on hold without a reason
Repro Steps:
1. Customers, open C140, tick Billing hold, leave the reason empty, save.
Expected: Enter a reason for the billing hold.
Actual: error page
Resolution: A hold needs a reason, as on the project page.
